definition: A specific nucleotide or protein sequence reported with an accession or isolate identifier, from which mutations and phylogeny are computed.
One or more specific nucleotide or amino-acid substitutions identified in a filovirus genome or protein relative to a reference.
Quantitative evidence of natural selection (dN/dS, FEL/MEME/RELAX, or equivalent) acting on a coding region or site.
Placement of an isolate within a phylogenetic tree, lineage assignment, or evidence of evolutionary relatedness among filoviruses.
Evidence of recombination, reassortment, or segment exchange in filoviral genomes.
Reported lethality, case-fatality, or virulence of a strain/variant in humans or animal models, independent of causal mutation attribution.
A specific mutation experimentally or clinically causally linked to altered virulence, tropism, immune escape, or pathogenicity — the direct label source for the pathogenicity predictor.
Epidemiological characterization of an outbreak: size, source, transmission chains, geographic spread.
Clinical signs, symptoms, disease course, or hematological/biochemical findings in infected hosts.
Environmental persistence, shedding, or transmission dynamics of the virus.
Evidence of host receptor engagement (e.g. NPC1), GP proteolytic activation (cathepsin), or cell entry determinants.
Molecular function of a filoviral protein (NP, VP35, VP40, GP, VP30, VP24, L), including polymerase activity, matrix assembly, or transcription.
Mechanisms by which the virus evades or antagonizes the host immune response (e.g. IFN antagonism by VP35/VP24), including antibody escape.
Evidence concerning the GP transcriptional editing site that generates sGP, GP, gp1,2, or ssGP.
Three-dimensional structural evidence (X-ray, cryo-EM, NMR) or epitope mapping for a filoviral protein or complex.
Identification or characterization of natural reservoir hosts (notably bats), zoonotic origin, or host-range determinants.
Host proteins or pathways demonstrated as required for, or restrictive of, filovirus infection.
A compound identified from a high-throughput or phenotypic antiviral screen with demonstrated activity against a filovirus.
Neutralizing antibody (monoclonal or polyclonal) potency, breadth, or the epitope residues they target.
A viral protein, host factor, or pathway proposed or validated as a therapeutic target for filovirus intervention.
siRNA, shRNA, or antisense/morpholino oligo knockdown evidence of reduced filovirus replication.
